contract_plain_english: For any random variable X, form Z by doubling X and subtracting one. Then X is a fair 0-or-1 Bernoulli variable exactly when Z is a fair -1-or-1 symmetric Bernoulli (Rademacher) variable. The source asserts both directions of this equivalence and nothing from the following Hoeffding theorem.

source_evidence.observation: The chapter explicitly glosses a Bernoulli random variable with parameter 1/2 as taking the values 0 and 1 with probability 1/2 each.
A symmetric Bernoulli distribution, also called a Rademacher distribution, is defined by the two values -1 and 1, each having probability 1/2.

binders: X: a numerical random variable on an implicit probability space.
Z: the random variable defined from X by the affine relation Z = 2X - 1.
conclusions: X has the usual Bernoulli distribution with parameter 1/2 if and only if Z has the symmetric Bernoulli, equivalently Rademacher, distribution.
Both directions are asserted: Bernoulli(1/2) for X implies symmetric Bernoulli for 2X - 1, and symmetric Bernoulli for 2X - 1 implies Bernoulli(1/2) for X.
definitions_and_conventions: Usual Bernoulli distribution with parameter 1/2 means that the variable takes values 0 and 1 with probability 1/2 each.
Symmetric Bernoulli distribution and Rademacher distribution are synonymous in this passage.
Symmetric Bernoulli distribution means that the variable takes values -1 and 1 with probability 1/2 each.
Z is not an unrelated second random variable: it is fixed to be the affine transform 2X - 1.
implicit_context: The probability space and measurability data are left implicit by the source.
The claim concerns one random variable and its deterministic affine transform; no independence or identical-distribution assumption is inherited from the surrounding discussion of sums.

undebatable_constraints: The statement must retain an if-and-only-if equivalence.
The input-side distribution is the usual Bernoulli distribution with parameter exactly 1/2, supported at 0 and 1 with equal probabilities.
The output-side distribution is the symmetric Bernoulli or Rademacher distribution, supported at -1 and 1 with equal probabilities.
The transformed variable must be Z = 2X - 1; changing the scale, shift, sign, or direction of the affine map changes the stated claim.
Z must remain the deterministic affine transform of the same X, not an independently chosen variable.
No independence hypothesis, family of random variables, or Hoeffding-type bound belongs to this selected passage.
